events.title: Baghdad surrenders to the Mongols
events.description: After a short siege, the Abbasid Caliph al-Musta'sim surrendered Baghdad to Hulagu Khan. The city was sacked and the Caliph executed days later, ending five centuries of Abbasid rule from Baghdad.
events.html: After a short siege, the Abbasid Caliph al-Musta'sim surrendered Baghdad to Hulagu Khan. The city was sacked and the Caliph executed days later, ending five centuries of Abbasid rule from Baghdad.

events.title: Robert the Bruce kills John Comyn at Dumfries
events.description: Bruce stabbed his rival for the Scottish crown before the altar of Greyfriars church. Committed to rebellion, he was crowned King of Scots weeks later and defeated the English at Bannockburn in 1314.
events.html: Bruce stabbed his rival for the Scottish crown before the altar of Greyfriars church. Committed to rebellion, he was crowned King of Scots weeks later and defeated the English at Bannockburn in 1314.

events.title: Treaty of Paris ends the Seven Years' War
events.description: France ceded Canada and lands east of the Mississippi to Britain, and Spain gave up Florida. Britain emerged as the leading colonial power, though France kept its trading posts in India.
events.html: France ceded Canada and lands east of the Mississippi to Britain, and Spain gave up Florida. Britain emerged as the leading colonial power, though France kept its trading posts in India.

events.title: Queen Victoria marries Prince Albert
events.description: Victoria married her cousin Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha at the Chapel Royal, St James's Palace. Her white wedding dress set a lasting fashion; Albert became her closest adviser.
events.html: Victoria married her cousin Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha at the Chapel Royal, St James's Palace. Her white wedding dress set a lasting fashion; Albert became her closest adviser.

events.title: HMS Dreadnought is launched
events.description: King Edward VII launched the battleship at Portsmouth. With ten 12-inch guns and steam turbines, she made existing battleships obsolete and intensified the naval race with Germany.
events.html: King Edward VII launched the battleship at Portsmouth. With ten 12-inch guns and steam turbines, she made existing battleships obsolete and intensified the naval race with Germany.

events.title: Soviet Union begins mass deportations from eastern Poland
events.description: The NKVD deported some 140,000 Polish citizens, many of them families of settlers and foresters, to Siberia and Kazakhstan. It was the first of four mass deportations in 1940-41.
events.html: The NKVD deported some 140,000 Polish citizens, many of them families of settlers and foresters, to Siberia and Kazakhstan. It was the first of four mass deportations in 1940-41.

events.title: U-2 pilot Gary Powers exchanged for Soviet spy Rudolf Abel
events.description: On the Glienicke Bridge between West Berlin and Potsdam, the US pilot shot down in 1960 was swapped for the KGB colonel Rudolf Abel. The bridge became known for Cold War exchanges.

events.title: Ron Brown becomes the first Black chairman of a major US party
events.description: Ron Brown was elected chairman of the Democratic National Committee. He helped Bill Clinton win in 1992 and became Secretary of Commerce before dying in a plane crash in 1996.
